2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.

13	#include <string>

18	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
19	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
20	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
21	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
22	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F9 contract: `run --model hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
3	# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the csr | pc | icount
4	# triggers. Three layers:
5	#
6	#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
7	#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
8	#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
9	#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
10	#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
11	#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
12	#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
13	#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
14	#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
15	#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
16	#
17	# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
18	# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
19	# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
20	set -uo pipefail
21	
22	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
23	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
24	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
25	
26	BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
27	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
28	CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
29	SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
30	ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default
31	
32	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
33	
34	# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
35	for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
36	  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
37	    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
38	done
39	echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"
40	
41	# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
42	# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
43	expect() {
44	  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
45	  local out rc
46	  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
47	  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
48	  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
49	}
50	expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
51	expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
52	expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
53	expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
54	  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
55	expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
56	expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
57	expect 2 'csr or pc'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount \
58	  --kanata /tmp/k "$SPIN"
59	expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr \
60	  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
61	echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"
62	
63	# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
64	QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
65	SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
66	PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
67	if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
68	  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
69	  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
70	  # the number's position is identical).
71	  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
72	  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
73	    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
74	    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
75	    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
76	    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
77	  }
78	
79	  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
80	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
81	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
82	  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
83	    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
84	  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
85	    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
86	  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"
87	
88	  # csr on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
89	  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
90	  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
91	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
92	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
93	  check_parity csr-c "$GO" "$AO"
94	
95	  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
96	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
97	        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
98	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
99	        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
100	  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"
101	
102	  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
103	  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
104	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
105	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
106	  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"
107	
108	  # kanata ROI trace forwards onto the vsim leg and writes a non-empty file.
109	  KAN=$(mktemp); rm -f "$KAN"
110	  timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" \
111	    --kanata "$KAN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1
112	  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after csr run"
113	  echo "[ok] kanata: csr run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
114	  rm -f "$KAN"
115	else
116	  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
117	fi
118	
119	ok "F9 run --model hybrid (csr|pc|icount)"

2	//
3	// One rule: the caller asks for `size` bytes; we honor HSIM_MMAP_DIR (else
4	// /dev/shm), statvfs-check free space, allocate a sparse file with
5	// mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line. No fallback chain, no
6	// filesystem-type probing. (The HSIM_MMAP_DIR name and "[hsim mmap]" status
7	// line stay verbatim with the Python golden until the F14 rename.)
8	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP

13	namespace andes_sim {

15	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
16	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
17	// to the argparse-style message. Mirrors hsim_shm.parse_size (fractional values
18	// truncate, like Python int(float(num) * mult)).
19	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);

22	// validate it can hold size + 256 MiB. Returns the directory on success; on
23	// failure returns "" and sets `err`. Mirrors hsim_shm.select_mmap_dir.
24	std::string select_mmap_dir(long long size, std::string& err);

27	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line, and
28	// return its path. On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file's
29	// lifetime (unlink when done). Mirrors hsim_shm.allocate.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
3	#
4	# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
5	# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
6	# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
7	# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
8	# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.
9	
10	# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
11	#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
12	#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
13	# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
14	# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
15	resolve_pc() {
16	  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
17	  case "$boundary" in
18	    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
19	    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
20	  esac
21	}
22	
23	# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
24	#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
25	#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
26	#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
27	#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
28	roi_resolve_pair() {
29	  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
30	  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
31	  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
32	  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
33	    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
34	    return 1
35	  fi
36	  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
37	  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
38	  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
39	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
40	    return 1
41	  fi
42	  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
43	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
44	    return 1
45	  fi
46	  return 0
47	}
48	
49	# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
50	#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the milmb ROI markers a fixture
51	#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
52	#     ENTER = the entry marker     `csrwi milmb,0`  (encoding 7c005073)
53	#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker  `csrwi milmb,1`  (encoding 7c00d073)
54	#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
55	#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
56	#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
57	#   CSR mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT keeps
58	#   the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison `csrwi milmb,1`
59	#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
60	#   dead one. The encodings are unambiguous (csr 0x7c0, uimm 0/1), so the
61	#   raw-bytes match needs no CSR-name table from objdump.
62	#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
63	#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
64	#   per-fixture config; ./hsim run still passes explicit boundaries.
65	roi_markers_from_disasm() {
66	  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
67	    $2 == "7c005073" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
68	    $2 == "7c00d073"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
69	    END {
70	      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
71	      else                              { exit 1 }
72	    }
73	  '
74	}
75

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
3	#
4	# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
5	# (build/andes-sim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
6	# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
7	# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
8	#
9	# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
10	# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
11	set -uo pipefail
12	
13	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
14	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
15	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
16	
17	GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim}"        # Python reference driver
18	NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test
19	
20	pass=0
21	fail=0
22	
23	# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
24	# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
25	# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
26	compare() {
27	  local name="$1"
28	  shift
29	  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
30	  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
31	  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
32	  g_rc=$?
33	  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
34	  n_rc=$?
35	  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
36	    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
37	    fail=$((fail + 1))
38	    return
39	  fi
40	  pass=$((pass + 1))
41	}
42	
43	# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
44	# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
45	# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
46	# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
47	compare_carried() {
48	  local name="$1"
49	  shift
50	  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
51	  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
52	  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
53	  g_rc=$?
54	  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
55	  n_rc=$?
56	  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
57	  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
58	    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
59	    fail=$((fail + 1))
60	    return
61	  fi
62	  pass=$((pass + 1))
63	}
64	
65	# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
66	compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
67	compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
68	compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
69	for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
70	  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
71	done
72	
73	echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
74	[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

2	# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
3	# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
4	#
5	#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
6	#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
7	#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
8	#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
9	#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
10	#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
11	#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
12	#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
13	#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
14	#      this exercises the exact argv path.
15	#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
16	#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
17	#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
18	#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
19	#      the deterministic proof.
20	set -uo pipefail
21	
22	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
23	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
24	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
25	
26	BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
27	RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"
28	
29	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
30	
31	# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
32	[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
33	"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"
34	
35	# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
36	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
37	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
38	
39	# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
40	# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
41	mkengine() {
42	  local f="$1/$2"
43	  cat >"$f" <<EOF
44	#!/bin/sh
45	if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
46	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"verilator","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
47	else
48	  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
49	fi
50	EOF
51	  chmod +x "$f"
52	}
53	
54	D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
55	mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
56	mkengine "$D1" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
57	mkengine "$D2" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
58	mkengine "$D2" v2 "verilator:v2" cycle-accurate m2
59	mkengine "$DF" f0 "verilator:f0" functional    fm
60	
61	# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
62	expect() {
63	  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
64	  local out rc
65	  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
66	  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
67	  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
68	}
69	
70	# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
71	expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
72	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
73	# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
74	expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*verilator:v1.*verilator:v2' \
75	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
76	# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
77	expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
78	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v1 dummy.elf
79	expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
80	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v2 dummy.elf
81	# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
82	expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
83	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
84	# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for accurate
85	expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
86	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:f0 dummy.elf
87	# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
88	expect 2 "no engine 'verilator:nope'" \
89	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:nope dummy.elf
90	# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
91	expect 2 'missing ELF' \
92	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate
93	expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
94	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate a.elf b.elf
95	# 2h. a CLI arg error is reported before (and instead of) engine discovery:
96	# missing ELF wins even when no engine exists, rather than "no cycle-accurate
97	# engine" -- so a typo never pays for a --describe subprocess per build.
98	expect 2 'missing ELF' \
99	  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate
100	echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"
101	
102	# 3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort)
103	SIM=$(ls "$ROOT"/verilator/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
104	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
105	if [ -n "$SIM" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
106	  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
107	  # The current fixtures are hybrid-oriented and loop forever standalone (no
108	  # exit path without QEMU's semihosting), so this caps the attempt: a cycle
109	  # line confirms the done-when; a timeout (rc 124) only confirms vsim launched
110	  # and is running, which is still useful. Either way -> not a failure. The cap
111	  # is short: the cycle line, if it comes, comes right after launch; otherwise
112	  # we are just confirming launch, so there is no point waiting longer.
113	  out=$(timeout 10 "$BIN" run --model accurate ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
114	  if echo "$out" | grep -Eq "[0-9]+ cycles simulated"; then
115	    echo "[ok] real accurate: vsim ran '$ELF' from reset, printed its cycle line (rc=$rc)"
116	  elif [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then
117	    echo "[skip] real accurate: vsim launched but did not finish in 10s (expected: standalone-from-reset of a hybrid fixture has no exit path)"
118	  else
119	    echo "[skip] real accurate: vsim exited rc=$rc with no cycle line (standalone-from-reset of a hybrid fixture is env-dependent)"
120	  fi
121	else
122	  echo "[skip] real accurate run: no built sim_* and/or fixture ($SIM / $ELF)"
123	fi

125	ok "F8 run --model accurate"

I have a complete picture. Here is the REUSE review of the F9 change set.

## REUSE findings

### 1. STRONG - `expect()` duplicated verbatim between f8 and f9 test scripts
- File: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f9.sh:43-49` (also `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f8.sh:62-68`)
- The two `expect()` definitions are byte-identical except `echo "$out"` (f8) vs `printf '%s\n' "$out"` (f9):
  ```
  expect() { local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2; out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
    [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail ...; ... grep -Eq "$re" || fail ... }
  ```
- Cost: ~7 lines of an rc+regex assertion helper duplicated across two sibling scripts.
- Fix: hoist `expect()` into `tests/lib/` (e.g. add to `tests/lib/log.sh`, which both already source, next to `fail`/`ok`). `log.sh`'s own header notes it exists precisely because `fail`/`ok` were "duplicated byte-identically in 20+ test scripts" - the same rationale applies here. Then `expect()` drops out of both f8 and f9.

### 2. MINOR - f9 re-hardcodes the qemu/vsim/plugin artifact paths that `paths.sh` centralizes
- File: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f9.sh:64-66`
  ```
  QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
  SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  ```
- These three literals are exactly the defaults `tests/lib/paths.sh::hybrid_resolve_paths()` assigns to `VSIM_QEMU` / `VSIM_BIN` / `VSIM_PLUGIN`.
- Cost: the artifact-path layout is duplicated; a future relocation must touch f9 too.
- Caveat (why I rank it minor): `hybrid_resolve_paths()` hard-exits 77 on a missing artifact, but f9 deliberately wants a *soft* skip (print `[skip]`, still call `ok`). So only the path literals are reusable, not the function as-is. Worth at most sourcing `paths.sh` for `TOP_ROOT` + the path defaults; full reuse of the resolver would change the skip semantics. Note the andes_sim f0-f8 family also doesn't source paths.sh, so the manual `ROOT` dance itself is the established sibling convention - leave that.

### 3. VERY MINOR - 128 MiB mmap default duplicated as a bare literal
- File: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:147` (`128LL * 1024 * 1024`), same literal in `driver/plan_itest.cpp:47`.
- No existing named constant to call, so this is "extract a shared constant," not "call an existing helper." Flagging only because the magic number now lives in two `.cpp` files both commenting "matches tests/e2e.sh." Low priority.

## Clean for reuse (the big-ticket items - no duplication)

- `driver/elf_syms.cpp/.hpp` - genuinely new. Grep for `Elf64|elf.h|SHT_SYMTAB|st_value` across `driver/ tests/ include/` finds no other C++ ELF reader; the only siblings are the bash `nm` path in `tests/lib/roi.sh` + `e2e.sh`, which aren't callable from C++. It is a deliberate cross-language port of `roi.sh:resolve_pc`, correctly reading `.symtab` directly. Nothing to reuse.
- `driver/cmd_run.cpp::run_hybrid` reuses the right helpers throughout: `check_one_elf`, `parse_size` (shm.hpp), `resolve_accurate_engine` (F8 selector), `discover_engines`, and delegates the shared-mmap allocation to `run_plan` (which owns `allocate()` internally) - so no shm/engine/argv logic is re-implemented here. It also consumes `PlanResult.phases[*].mcycle` rather than re-parsing the drain file, so `state.hpp::read_state_file()` is not duplicated.
- `driver/hybrid.cpp` reuses `resolve_pc`; `hybrid_trigger` (CLI->Trigger) and `leg_trigger_args` (Trigger->argv) are complementary, not overlapping. `vsim_extra_args` is new with no prior equivalent.
- New CLI flags (`cli.cpp:64-71`) extend the existing `opts[]` table and reuse `match_opt` - the established pattern.
- `leg_trigger_args` / `Step.extra_args` thread through the existing `build_argv` path in `plan_argvs`; no argv assembly is reinvented.

No files were edited.
